cases.answer_preview:
На момент мая 2026 года официальной информации о релизе архитектуры "SAM 3" от Meta не обнаружено. Оригинальная модель **Segment Anything Model (SAM)**, представленная Meta, остается актуальной версией, доступной в [официальном репозитории на GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything). Эта модель обучена на наборе данных SA-1B и демонстрирует сильные способности к сегментации объектов в условиях нулевого обучения.

Вместо SAM 3, в научном сообществе активно развиваются гибридные архитектуры на основе SAM. Ярким примером является **SAM-Mamba**, представленный в статье IEEE WACV 2025. Эта модель объединяет SAM с фреймворком Mamba для улучшения сегментации полипов в медицинск

citations.snippet:
- The paper addresses limitations in standard multimodal pretraining paradigms, such as contrastive learning on large image-text datasets, which optimize for zero-shot transfer but do not explicitly support few-shot adaptation.
- The authors propose a novel approach called Context-Aware Multimodal Pretraining (CAMP) that enhances representation learning by incorporating contextual information to improve few-shot adaptation capabilities.
- CAMP introduces a context-aware mechanism during pretraining that leverages both global and local context from image-text pairs, enabling models to better generalize to new tasks with limited labeled data.
- The method is evaluated on standard benchmarks for few-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval, demonstrating consistent improvements over baseline methods that rely on standard contrastive learning.
- Experimental results show that context-aware pretraining leads to more robust and adaptable multimodal representations, bridging the gap between zero-shot and few-shot performance in downstream tasks.

The article is authored by Aarti Ahirwar and Ritu Tandon from SAGE University, Indore, India.

According to the metadata and abstract, the paper presents a review of the shift in Visual Document Understanding (VDU) from traditional OCR-dependent, multi-stage processing pipelines to OCR-free, end-to-end multimodal transformer models. It highlights how reliance on off-the-shelf OCR tools introduces error propagation, undermining downstream natural language processing (NLP) tasks. The paper examines architectural advancements, including Layout-aware Transformers, Vision Transformers (ViT), hierarchical models like Swin, and generative frameworks such as Donut and Pix2Struct, which directly map pixel inputs to structured outputs without intermediate OCR steps.

The authors analyze key technical challenges in this domain—specifically the high-resolution input bottleneck and cross-modal alignment—and evaluate state-of-the-art performance on standard VDU benchmarks. They also discuss future research directions, particularly in the context of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), with implications for understanding complex document layouts and structured data such as tables and charts.
